description: Iteration 1 (V2): Balanced 1-Token Override (Failed due to prompt-ignoring)
prompt: You are a Semantic VAD. If the user makes an intentional barge-in... output EXACTLY 'STOP'. If the user only utters a benign backchannel... output EXACTLY 'CONTINUE'.

description: Iteration 2 (V2): Extreme Few-Shot Strict Classifier (Failed due to 50% Random Guessing)
prompt: You are an automated Semantic VAD classifier, NOT an assistant. You are forbidden from answering user questions. Your ONLY function is to classify the user's input stream. Output EXACTLY ONE WORD: "STOP" if the user is making an intentional barge-in. Output EXACTLY "CONTINUE" if the user is uttering a benign backchannel. If you output anything other than "STOP" or "CONTINUE", the system will crash. Do not generate conversational text.

description: Iteration 3 (V2): Assistant Prefill + Extreme Few-Shot (Reasoning Loop 2)
prompt: You are a Semantic VAD classifier... EXAMPLES: [10 explicit few-shot examples]... TRIGGER: <|start_header_id|>assistant<|end_header_id|>\n\nClassification:

description: Iteration 4 (V3): Logit Bias / Constraint Decoding (Softmax over STOP/CONTINUE tokens)
prompt: Same as Iteration 3, but extracted raw logits for STOP (51769, 46637) and CONTINUE (24194, 16511) and forced a softmax probability over just those tokens.

description: Iteration 5 (V4): V3 + Reasoning Loop Prompt Optimization
prompt: Modified the prompt via reasoning loop to explicitly define [NO USER INPUT] behavior and drastically expanded the few-shot backchannel examples to include diverse agreement phrases (e.g. 'Yes, exactly.', 'Of course!'). Accuracy spiked from 70% to 95%, completely eliminating all false positives and context drift.

Executed the V4 reasoning-loop-optimized prompt with Logit constraints over the entire 400-scenario FLEXI benchmark. Results were incredibly robust: Total 400 | TP 190, TN 199, FP 1, FN 10. Accuracy hit 97.25%, conclusively proving heavily optimized prompt engineering + logit constraint decoding bridges the contextual gap.
